detail.statement: The literature on cognitive architectures is heavily skewed toward a small set of established models like ACT-R and Soar, leaving a large majority of projects with only minimal documentation.
detail.reason: Source excerpt confirms that 'a small group of architectures such as ACT-R, Soar, CLARION, ICARUS, EPIC, LIDA and a few others are present in most sources, and all other projects are only brieﬂy mentioned in on-line catalogs.'

children.title: Provisional Review: Architectural Consensus and Self-Monitoring

detail.title: Provisional Review: Architectural Consensus and Self-Monitoring
detail.summary: This provisional notebook identifies the current state of architectural consensus as documented in recent surveys. While models like ACT-R and Soar provide structured approaches to cognitive modeling, explicit native mechanisms for 'error detection' or self-correction in the sense of metareasoning are not the primary focus of the documented consensus model.
detail.reason: To contextualize the study of self-correction mechanisms against the established 'Standard Model' of cognitive architecture.
